title: Load Factor Scale on Noticed C&I Termination Damages
content:
For Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts, the damages rate of a noticed termination is scaled by the facility's load factor, the twelve months' kWh divided by the product of the capacity tag on the most recently posted capacity charge line and 8760 hours per year: a load factor of 0.70 or more scales it by 0.90, a load factor from 0.50 up to below 0.70 scales it by 0.95, and a lower load factor, or no capacity charge line, leaves it unscaled. Scaling multiplies the damages rate per kWh by the figure shown.

- **The twelve months' kWh** are the kWh on the contract's supply lines posted in the twelve months before the handling date. A line falls in the twelve months before the handling date when it was posted on or before the handling date and fewer than twelve whole calendar months have passed from its posted date to the handling date, a month being complete on the same day of the month as the posted date.
- **The capacity tag** is the tag in kW shown on the contract's capacity charge line with the latest posted date.

| Load factor | Damages rate multiplied by |
|---|---|
| 0.70 or more | 0.90 |
| 0.50 to below 0.70 | 0.95 |
| below 0.50 | 1, unscaled |
| no capacity charge line on the contract | 1, unscaled |

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Twelve months' kWh | Capacity tag | Tag multiplied by 8760 | Load factor | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3066000 | 500 kW | 4380000 | 0.70 | 0.90 |
| 2628000 | 500 kW | 4380000 | 0.60 | 0.95 |
| 1971000 | 500 kW | 4380000 | 0.45 | 1 |
| 2400000 | no capacity charge line | none | none | 1 |
